orphanDialog: bigone|A man in a long coat stopped the sundial for me. He said if the day never ended, you'd never pack up and go home.
boppy|He's a FISH, kiddo.
boppy|Marsh junk. Everything people drop out here ends up grumpy about it. Like me, at the DMV.
boppy|Now the water has drained, and the way to the Deep Pool is open. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.
boppy|Old Iron-Gill. Forty years, Dee. I TOLD everybody.
boppy|Old gold. Keep that in your pocket, Tom. Penny will want to hear about it. Penny wants to hear about everything.
boppy|Put the date. Put the time. Use the sundial. It works now.
boppy|Real as my heartburn, kiddo.
boppy|That's no perch. That's OLD IRON-GILL. I saw him in 1994! I TOLD everybody!
boppy|That's what I said.
boppy|The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. I saw it at Cattail Pier in 1994. Nobody believes me.
boppy|The old reeds. When I was a kid we said there was a sundial back in there that told the wrong time.
boppy|The sundial still says seven o'clock, no matter what time it is.
boppy|This is Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine, and it hasn't changed.
deedee|Back already! Look at you. Did they feed you out there? Never mind. I'll feed you.
deedee|Nobody believes him.
deedee|Thank you, Rosie. Now. Let me look at him.
grace|I have proof. It's in my notebook. With the time. From a sundial.
grace|It MOVED. Shadows don't move like that. I'm writing this down. In pen.
grace|It's the AFTERNOON. The sun is right there. Sundials can't be wrong. That's not how sundials work.
grace|Sundials can't tell the wrong time. That's not how sundials work.
narrator|Click. The shadow swings all the way around the dial and settles on the right hour.
narrator|Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. The bubbles look almost friendly.
narrator|Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. There used to be a boardwalk through here. Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.
narrator|The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. Behind it, the old reeds lean apart around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.
narrator|The kettle whistles, low and long. Oolong leans in to listen.
narrator|Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, then drains away to mud. The way to the Deep Pool is open.
oolong|The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny's shop. He pays double, and he never takes his hat off.
rose|Boppy, is the Whisker Perch real?
rose|Tata! Something shiny is stuck in it!
tom|It works because I took the coin out. A man in a long coat stops a sundial so a lonely fish can keep his company. That's a strange favor to do for a fish.
tom|It's a gold coin, wedged right under the pointer. That's what was holding the shadow at seven. Somebody pushed this in on purpose.
tom|On Long Island? Nobody here pays double for anything.
oolong|The kettle is still going on about that man in the long coat. Gold coins. Paying double.
